newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures close sharply down, more spec selling.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures close sharply down, more spec selling.

text.p: FCOJ futures ended down for the ninth consecutive day, prompting several analysts to wonder if support exists in this seemingly bottomless market.
"It's unusual that we are down so many days in row...and confirms there is no support," an analyst said, adding that several technical indicators are oversold and nearing zero.
Indeed, the market sank to life-of-contract lows across the board on early technically-driven selling by the speculators.
Prices recouped some losses in the afternoon but remained weaker as the trade took to the sidelines.
The analyst noted that the trade has already filled its needs for the season. While light scale-down trade buying was noted, it is not likely to provide firm support.
"The trade who stepped in to take long positions did so from higher levels and are pretty much bought out," she said.
March closed down 1.75 to 80.10, traded 82.00 to a new contract low of 79.25. Spot January eased 1.60 on the day to 76.50. The back months finished 2.15 lower to 0.35 higher.
Volume was estimated at a hefty 6,500 lots.
Support was pegged on the ten-year chart at 68.50, a low made in March 1993, and then at 65.45, a low made in Feb 1993.

Increasing open interest amid declining prices and robust volume signals ongoing technical weakness, analysts said. They said that ultimately, the speculators will buy back their short positions and provide temporary support.
But as one analyst put it: "Who knows where that will be?"
